Connor —

Quick legal read and proposal (high level):

- Credits: accept a simplified tier that mirrors Helios' linear intent but caps exposure. Proposed language: "For monthly uptime percentages below 99.9% and above 99.0%, Service Credits will be calculated on a linear pro-rata basis up to a maximum of 30% of monthly fees; credits across multiple regions for the same incident shall be aggregated and limited to 30% total." This preserves predictability for both sides.

- Maintenance windows: accept 4-hour planned windows per region with the following caveat: Planned windows may be scheduled in two-week notice blocks but Redwood reserves the right to combine or stagger adjacent regional windows to limit operational risk; such adjustments will be communicated 72 hours prior.

- Emergency carveouts: propose emergency patching language that allows "immediate action" for critical CVEs (severity >= 9) with notification as soon as practicable and a post-event report. For non-critical urgent patches, require 24 hours notice.

- Ops safeguards: include an explicit rollback & post-mortem obligation and a one-time mitigation credit (up to 5%) if an operational maintenance exceeds stated windows because of Redwood error.

I'll produce redline snippets and a clean counter-order form for Connor to send.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
